Highlight sub-regions across a stack of tracks

Source: R/highlight-stack.R
highlight_stack.Rd

Shades one or more sub-regions as unbroken bands running through every track of a stack, including the space between tracks. Bands cover each run of adjacent tracks that share the same coord_locus() or coord_loci() windows; other plots in the stack, such as the ideogram from plot_ideogram(), are left alone. Apply it as the last step, after the stack is assembled with patchwork.

Bands are drawn over the data by default, so they stay visible on tracks whose data covers the whole panel, like dense bed tracks. Adjust alpha to set how strongly they tint the data, or use layer = "below" to keep the data untinted.

Usage

highlight_stack(
  stack,
  regions,
  fill = NULL,
  alpha = 0.3,
  colour = NA,
  layer = c("above", "below"),
  tracks = NULL,
  show_legend = NULL,
  legend_title = "Highlight"
)

Arguments

stack

A patchwork of tracks, e.g. from patchwork::wrap_plots(..., ncol = 1), or a single ggplot.

regions

Regions to highlight as one of:

  • A character vector of windows, e.g. "chr3:187744872-187744917". Names, if given, are used as labels.

  • A data frame with start and end columns and optional seqnames, label, and fill columns.

  • A GRanges object, with optional label and fill metadata columns.

fill

Fill colors, either one color for all regions or one per label (named or in order of appearance). Ignored if regions has a fill column. By default a single region is orange and labeled regions use a hue palette.

alpha

Opacity of the bands, default: 0.3

colour

Outline color of the bands, default: none

layer

Draw the bands "above" (default) or "below" the track data.

tracks

Positions of the plots in the stack to cover, e.g. 3:5. By default all plots using coord_locus() or coord_loci(). Bands still run unbroken through adjacent tracks.

show_legend

Add a legend of the region labels, default: TRUE when regions are labeled.

legend_title

Title of the legend, default: "Highlight"

Value

A gtable of the highlighted stack with class highlighted_stack. Print it to draw, save it with ggplot2::ggsave(), or wrap it with patchwork::wrap_elements(full = ) to combine with other plots.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
win <- "chr3:187744850-187745350"

stack <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
  plot_ideogram(win, flank = 250),
  ggplot2::ggplot(snvs) + geom_mutation_count() + coord_locus(win, 250) +
    theme_genomic(x_axis = "ticks"),
  ggplot2::ggplot() + geom_gene_track(genes_of_interest = "BCL6") +
    coord_locus(win, 250) + theme_genomic(y_axis = "blank"),
  ncol = 1, guides = "collect")

highlight_stack(stack,
                c("Normal MBC Hotspot 1" = "chr3:187744872-187744917",
                  "Normal MBC Hotspot 2" = "chr3:187745199-187745246",
                  "DLBCL Hotspot" = "chr3:187744678-187744698"),
                fill = c("#9BD08A", "#C2EFB4", "#DC766F"),
                legend_title = "Windows")
} # }
